proposal: The Mandate recommends eliminating DOE's energy and water efficiency standards for appliances, and says Congress should modify or repeal the underlying law. Before or instead of repeal, DOE should use the statute's existing limits, such as prioritizing only standards with large savings, avoiding rules whose benefits do not justify the cost, and preserving product features and quality.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 DOE has not rescinded any existing appliance or equipment efficiency standard by final rule, and its May 2025 proposals to rescind or withdraw standards for more than a dozen product types remain non-final in Federal Register queries. Congress, using the Congressional Review Act, nullified three rules finalized late in the previous administration that would have tightened standards (walk-in coolers and freezers, commercial refrigerators and freezers, and consumer gas-fired instantaneous water heaters), so those amended standards have no effect, and DOE repealed the showerhead definition in 10 CFR 430.2 in a rule published 2025-04-15. Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) set a policy of protecting consumer choice among appliances. DOE finalized a withdrawal of its miscellaneous gas products coverage determination on 2025-05-07 (a coverage determination, not a standard), published the proposed rescissions on 2025-05-16, formally withdrew the three disapproved standards rules on 2025-05-20, and removed provisions of a fourth disapproved rule on 2025-09-09. In 2026 DOE finalized determinations leaving small electric motor and metal halide fixture standards unchanged (2026-02-13), and on 2026-07-07 it proposed revising its Process Rule and requested comment on its analytic methods; the Process Rule comment period was extended to 2026-08-21. The Mandate's statutory step (modify or repeal the Energy Policy and Conservation Act standards program) has not been taken.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 states a policy of protecting Americans' choice among appliances and directs agencies to review and begin plans to suspend, revise or rescind actions that restrict that choice.

DOE publishes a final rule (90 FR 19250, effective 2025-06-06) withdrawing its 2022 determination that miscellaneous gas products, including decorative hearths and outdoor heaters, are covered products and removing their definitions from 10 CFR 430.2; DOE cites Executive Orders 14192 and 14154 as consistent with the action. This is a coverage determination, not a standard.

DOE publishes a batch of proposed rescissions and withdrawals of standards, test procedures and coverage determinations; the battery charger notice proposes removing the standard at 10 CFR 430.32(z) on a tentative finding that no standard is economically justified, with comments due 2025-07-15, and cites Executive Orders 14154 and 14192 as policy alignment. A law firm counts more than a dozen product types and says all are proposals, not final actions.

DOE withdraws three standards rules that Congress disapproved under the Congressional Review Act: commercial refrigerators and freezers (rule of 2025-01-21), consumer gas-fired instantaneous water heaters (rule of 2024-12-26) and walk-in coolers and walk-in freezers (rule of 2024-12-23); the walk-in notice is the cited example and the other two are separate Federal Register documents of the same date.
DOE removes the certification, labeling and enforcement provisions of an October 2024 appliance rule that Congress disapproved under the Congressional Review Act.
DOE publishes final determinations that more stringent standards for small electric motors and for metal halide lamp fixtures are not cost-effective, so the standards are not amended.

DOE proposes revising its Process Rule (91 FR 42034; making Appendix A binding for certain actions, defining significant energy savings, adding economic thresholds, reinstating the walk-up comparison and the clear and convincing evidence description) and separately requests comment on its analytic methods for setting standards; on 2026-07-28 the Process Rule comment deadline is extended from 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-21.

DOE issues a notice that its 2022 manufactured housing energy standards have no legal effect under the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (Pub. L. 119-101, enacted 2026-07-11) until HUD adopts standards, and says it will not enforce them. This is a separate DOE program from the consumer product and equipment standards the Mandate discusses.

DOE publishes a final rule (91 FR 64105, effective 2026-12-07) withdrawing the optional appendix B (TE2) test procedure for commercial warm air furnaces, which would have applied only to future TE2-based standards, and keeping the appendix A test; DOE cites test burden outweighing uncertain benefits, Executive Order 14192 and its proposed Process Rule's preference for industry test procedures, and states no existing standard is changed.

title: Eliminate or curb DOE appliance and equipment efficiency standards
uncertainties: The finding that the May 2025 proposals are not final rests on a Federal Register API query of DOE final rules published since 2025-05-01 with the term Energy Conservation Program, which returned 13 rules (the 2025-05-07 coverage withdrawal, three 2025-05-20 withdrawals of disapproved rules and a 2025-05-20 central air conditioner test procedure delay, two 2025-09-09 rules, two 2026-02-13 determinations, a 2026-04-14 rescission of legacy grant program regulations, and 2026 rules on external power supplies, manufactured housing and commercial furnace test procedures), none of which finalizes a rescission of a standard; a final action filed under an unexpected title could be missed. A matching proposed-rule query was too long to run. The showerhead definition repeal (2025-04-15), the 2025-05-16 product list beyond the battery charger notice, and the 2026-03-31 fluorescent ballast, 2026-04-27 petition and 2026-06-15 distribution transformer notices were seen as listings and abstracts only. The Process Rule proposal text was read to about 100,000 characters of 125,602, and its visible text does not say DOE will rescind standards. Which CRA resolution dates apply to each withdrawn rule was not checked. No lawsuit over the proposals was found, but court dockets were not searched. The manufactured housing statute is adjacent, not an appliance standards repeal. Independent review of 2026-10-16: the API listing was re-run and again shows 13 final rules with no final rescission of an existing standard. The 2025-07-15 comments by a coalition of states, the District of Columbia and New York City opposing the May 2025 proposals were moved here from the timeline because they rest only on a law-firm alert, which also said lawsuits appeared likely.
